rationale: The Ollama GPU resource management problem is technically real and affects a growing segment of developer/ML power users, but the buyer is mixed (hobbyists plus professionals) with almost no willingness to pay — Ollama itself is free and open source, and users expect GPU tooling to be free or OS-level. More critically, the solution requires system-level GPU/VRAM management code (CUDA context manipulation, process suspension) that is completely outside what Claude plus a landing page and Stripe can build. Both buildability_with_ai (2) and operational_autonomy (2) fail their gates by a wide margin.
solution_plan: A solo non-technical operator absolutely cannot build this. GPU VRAM pause/resume requires low-level CUDA or driver-level code — it's a systems programming problem, not a prompt engineering problem. Even if outsourced to engineers, the target users (developers running Ollama) expect this kind of tool to be free and open-source, not a paid subscription. There is no viable micro-service angle here for this factory. Drop entirely.
notes: Fails buildability_with_ai (2 < 6 floor), operational_autonomy (2 < 7 floor), buyer_clarity (4 < 6 floor), and willingness_to_pay (3 < 5 floor). All four build gates fail. Total 3.4 well below min_total_to_validate.
